messages:
customer-ops: Hey team — customer on private VPC seeing intermittent inference stream resets when hitting our hosted endpoint. Symptoms: streaming responses cut off ~30-120s in, client sees ECONNRESET and TLS handshake fails on retry. Happened after recent firewall hardening.
sam: Thanks — can you paste the exact error and a short repro? Which deployment (Private/Dedicated)?
customer-ops: Private (VPC), behind customer-managed FW and NACL. Repro steps:
1) curl -v --http1.1 https://inference.redwood.example.com/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' --data-binary @prompt.json
2) stream starts, then mid-response we get: "recv error: Connection reset by peer". TLS logs show "fatal alert: handshake_failure" on second attempt.
jorge: Do you have tcpdump or packet traces? Need to know if SYN/ACKs are being dropped or if NAT translation is changing ports.
customer-ops: Pasted anonymized tcpdump snippet:
```
12:01:02.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 3.4.5.6.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
12:01:02.223457 IP 3.4.5.6.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
12:01:32.523789 IP 3.4.5.6.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [RST], seq 12345, ack 67890
```
maria: That RST nearly 30s after the handshake looks like a firewall state eviction or conntrack timeout. Do they have a stateful inspection device with a short TCP timeout? Also NACLs are stateless — if NACL denies return ephemeral ports later, you can get silent drops or RSTs.
customer-ops: Customer says NACL rules were tightened: allowed only ports 80,443 outbound and a tight ephemeral range excluded. Their NAT gateway does SNAT, but ephemeral range on return was narrowed. They also have a WAF/proxy doing deep-inspect.
niki: Two likely issues: 1) NACL is stateless — must allow ephemeral return port range (usually 32768-61000) for return traffic; 2) If there's a TCP terminating middlebox (proxy), keepalives or long-lived streams can be torn down if the device hit connection limits or aggressive timeouts. Quick check: ask them to run `ss -ntap | grep 443` and show conntrack entries `sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip>`.
sam: As a quick repro, can they temporarily widen NACL outbound/ingress to allow ephemeral range and test? Also try switching to dedicated NAT with preserved port mapping.
customer-ops: Will test — customer expanded NACL to allow 32768-61000 both directions and opened SG egress 0.0.0.0/0:443 temporarily. Repro now shows stable streams for 45m without resets.
jorge: Good signal. Follow-ups: (a) if they can't open full ephemeral range, they can restrict their source port range for SNAT (e.g., nat port pool => 50000-51000) and allow that in NACL; (b) check WAF/proxy session timeouts and TCP idle timeouts; (c) ensure TLS session resumption settings aren't causing full handshake failures on reconnect.
customer-ops: They prefer narrower surface: will allocate SNAT pool 50000-51000 and update NACL to allow that range. Also found this in proxy logs: "connection closed by firewall after 60s inactivity".
maria: Recommend client set TCP keepalive or use HTTP/2 ping/stream heartbeats so middleboxes see activity. For our side, add a KB link to troubleshooting: https://internal.redwood/docs/support/firewall-nat-ephemeral-ports
devops-bot: Reminder: run `nc -vz <inference-ip> 443` and `curl --resolve ... --http2` as smoke tests. Also file a follow-up if they want Redwood Private config review.
niki: I'll draft a short KB for customers: - explain ephemeral port return path, - show how to narrow SNAT pool, - show conntrack/netstat checks, - proxy timeout mitigation.
sam: Thanks everyone. Customer will confirm after NAT pool change and we can close. @customer-ops please ping when done.
customer-ops: Update: customer moved to SNAT 50000-50050 and whitelisted those ports in NACL+SG. Verified stable streaming for 2 hours, no TLS handshake failures. They're scheduling a firewall change window to make it permanent.
sam: Great — closing loop. Tips for postmortem: add explicit lines in Private onboarding to confirm ephemeral port mapping and recommended SNAT ranges. :white_check_mark:
